topic: Point-Slope and Two-Point Forms of a Line
title: Two Dots, One Road: Line Equations Explained Simply | Class 11 Maths
description:
Aarav puts two dots on a map, his home and his college. A straight road joins them, and he wants one rule that says whether any spot is on the road. Can two dots really describe a road that goes on forever? In this animated lesson for Class 11 Maths (NCERT Chapter 9, Straight Lines) we build the point-slope form and the two-point form of the equation of a line.

You will watch a point P slide along a line while the slope from a fixed point P0 stays at exactly one half, then see the slope change the moment P steps off the line. From that test we derive y - y0 = m(x - x0) step by step, turn two points into the two-point form, compare the two forms side by side, meet vertical and horizontal lines (x = a, y = b), and find the line through (1, -1) and (3, 5). Two pause-and-think questions, the exam trap with a negative coordinate, an original JEE Main pattern question with a full solution, a recap card and three questions to check yourself.

Follows the NCERT book. Useful for CBSE, ICSE (ISC), Karnataka PUC and other state boards, and JEE.

In this video:
0:00 Two dots on a map
0:25 What the equation of a line means
0:38 Live: slide a point along the line
1:11 The point-slope form, step by step
1:45 The two-point form
2:05 Point-slope vs two-point
2:42 Vertical and horizontal lines
3:14 Worked example: through (1, -1) and (3, 5)
3:51 Exam trap: x minus minus two
4:20 Practice question (JEE Main pattern)
5:01 Recap and three questions to answer

Next episode (Ep 72): Slope-Intercept and Intercept Forms of a Line. Where does the road cross the two main streets?
